text.p: Demand for the Megane Scenic, the innovative Renault car designed like a small minivan, has overwhelmed the French automaker, which has been forced to delay its launch in Spain and Britain.
"We were expecting a success with the Scenic but not like this. We expected demand to increase gradually, but the response has been immediate," a Renault spokeswoman said on Friday.
Renault, which had planned to launch the Scenic in Britain next month, has delayed its introduction until May, she said. The launch in Spain has been put off five months to June.
The car is scheduled to be launched on time in Germany next week, the spokeswoman said.

Delays in deliveries of the car, which carries a sticker price of 99,700 francs ($18,700), have stretched to 10 weeks in France, Italy, Belgium and other European countries where the Scenic was introduced in the autumn.
Renault has assembled a team to find ways to boost production of the bestseller, which was voted 1997 European Car of the Year in November by top motoring journalists.
The Scenic is produced at Renault's factory in Douai, which rolls out 700 models a day, while demand is running at around 900-1,000 models daily.
"We're studying more flexible work schedules to produce more cars on the same assembly line," the spokeswoman said.

As the Scenic is built on the same platform as the other Meganes -- a hatchback and coupe were launched in November 1995 and a sedan was introduced in October -- the company may adjust production rates of the different models.

Despite the complications resulting from the surge in demand, the Scenic's success is welcome news for Renault, which is the smallest of the Big Six carmakers and has been losing money on its car operations for more than a year.

Renault, which set a style trend a few years ago with the launch of the whimsical Twingo, conceived the Megane five-car family to help it expand its share of the biggest car market segment in Europe and to diversify sales.
Roughly half the cars it produces are compacts and small cars, which have the slimmest profit margins.

Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer has said the company will probably show a loss for 1996 after losing market share in France and Europe, but he said he was counting on the Meganes to boost sales and earnings this year.
The Scenic was launched in France in October. Renault plans to introduce the last model in the Megane family, a cabriolet, next year. ($ = 5.324 French Francs)
